You dont have to do a full teardown, but I would pull the heads and the oil pan. With the heads off you can check the cylinder walls and pistons to make sure they are in good shape and from the pan side see if there is any slop in the rods or crank. They flow well right to around 6000 and have a small combustion chamber so you can have higher compression. 58cc. If you dont do any performance work you will be better off with a 500cfm carb vs the one you have now. It will either be lazy or a pig on fuel. It can work, just not the best choice. Which edelbrock intake does it have? I hope a dual plane of some sort. If it is a single plane I would change it out. Single plane is good for high horsepower engines but a dog on the low end. Eps is a good budget intake to replace factory stuff, but an rpm air gap is a really good choice. Headers are cheap from summit racing and there are lots of options to fit your car. Long tube would be preferred. I would only get block huggers if you have a lot of clearance issues. Ps units hold up fairly well, I do not think I would ditch this unless something was wrong. I can understand getting rid of the ac. Do you have a serpinte belt or a v belt setup? It is easier to remove things from a v belt setup than a serpintine.
